title: Boss: three Windows tickets
summary: An empty reboot report, a scheduled task with Last Run Result 0x1, and a registry setting the agent ignores. Fix each WinOps function until its tests are green.

steps.title: The WinOps queue
body: Three tickets are open against the team's WinOps module (`Get-Content ~/src/WinOps/TICKETS.md`). Each one has
a test file in `~/src/WinOps/tests/` that describes the right behaviour, with the Windows cmdlets mocked. Read the
ticket, read the function, run the tests, fix the **function**. The checks run the original test files.

steps.title: OPS-3101: the reboot report is always empty
prompt: Run `Invoke-Pester ~/src/WinOps/tests/Get-RebootHistory.Tests.ps1 -Output Detailed`. Pester 6 prints the call it
recorded: compare its `StartTime` with today. Fix `~/src/WinOps/Public/Get-RebootHistory.ps1` (there is more than
one problem) until the tests pass.

checks.name: the Get-RebootHistory tests pass
checks.cmd: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -c '$r = Invoke-Pester "$env:DOJO_FILES/tests-boss/Get-RebootHistory.Tests.ps1" -PassThru -Output None; "$($r.PassedCount) of $($r.TotalCount) pass"; $r.Failed | ForEach-Object { "FAILED: $($_.ExpandedName): $($_.ErrorRecord.Exception.Message)" }'
checks.fail: Not all tests pass yet (the failing ones are listed).

checks.name: errors are not silenced
checks.fail: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` also hides *access denied* and *log not found*. Catch the one expected error (no events found) instead.

hints: `AddDays($Days)` is a week in the **future**: no event is newer than that. It should be `AddDays(-$Days)`.
The test wants the newest first: `Sort-Object TimeCreated -Descending`.
Replace `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` with `-ErrorAction Stop` inside `try`, and in `catch` return quietly only when the message starts with `No events were found`, else `throw`.
solution: Who restarted this server in the last -Days days, and why (event 1074).
steps.explain: `SilentlyContinue` made a wrong filter look like a quiet week. Distinguish *no data* (fine, report zero) from *could not read* (fail loudly): that is the difference between a report you can trust and one that is merely green. For unexpected shutdowns, add event 6008 to the same report.

steps.title: OPS-3107: Last Run Result 0x1
prompt: The morning report task fails with `0x1` (the script exited with 1) although the script works when run by hand in
`pwsh`. Read `~/src/WinOps/Public/Register-ReportTask.ps1` and the ticket, run its tests, and fix the function:
PowerShell 7, the path with its space quoted, `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`, still daily at 06:00.

checks.name: the Register-ReportTask tests pass
checks.cmd: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -c '$r = Invoke-Pester "$env:DOJO_FILES/tests-boss/Register-ReportTask.Tests.ps1" -PassThru -Output None; "$($r.PassedCount) of $($r.TotalCount) pass"; $r.Failed | ForEach-Object { "FAILED: $($_.ExpandedName): $($_.ErrorRecord.Exception.Message)" }'
checks.fail: Not all tests pass yet (the failing ones are listed).

hints: Three bugs in one line: `powershell.exe` is Windows PowerShell 5.1, which cannot parse `??`; `-File C:\Ops Scripts\...` without quotes is two arguments; and there is no `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`.
explain: On a real box, `Get-ScheduledTask 'Morning report' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Actions` shows what the task
actually runs, and `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo` its `LastTaskResult`. Add `Start-Transcript` at the top of scheduled
scripts: a task has no console, and the transcript is where the `??` parse error would have been visible at once.

steps.title: OPS-3112: the agent ignores Enabled
prompt: Two symptoms, one function: on a new server `Set-AgentConfig` fails because the key does not exist; on an old one
it "works" but the agent ignores the value. Fix `~/src/WinOps/Public/Set-AgentConfig.ps1` until
`Invoke-Pester ~/src/WinOps/tests/Set-AgentConfig.Tests.ps1` passes: create the key if needed, write `Enabled` as a

checks.name: the Set-AgentConfig tests pass
checks.cmd: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -c '$r = Invoke-Pester "$env:DOJO_FILES/tests-boss/Set-AgentConfig.Tests.ps1" -PassThru -Output None; "$($r.PassedCount) of $($r.TotalCount) pass"; $r.Failed | ForEach-Object { "FAILED: $($_.ExpandedName): $($_.ErrorRecord.Exception.Message)" }'
checks.fail: Not all tests pass yet (the failing ones are listed).

hints: The agent reads `Enabled` as a number; a `String` value `"1"` is a different type, so it is ignored.
`if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $key)) { New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null }` creates it (and missing parents).

`[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]`, then guard both changes with `$PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess(...)`, and write `New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name Enabled -PropertyType DWord -Value ([int]$Enabled) -Force`.
solution: Turns the monitoring agent on or off in the registry.
explain: For settings a whole fleet must have, Group Policy or Intune is the usual tool; a function like this is for
the cases they do not cover, or for an agent's own key. Either way: right value type, create what is missing, and
`-WhatIf` before you push it to 200 servers with `Invoke-Command`.
